results.title: Call for Papers: AI and Creativity in Cultural Industries
results.content: This Special Issue invites contributions that critically examine how AI is transforming creative processes, professional practices, and organizational models across sectors such as art, design, publishing, education, and cultural institutions. 🔍 Possible topics include: • AI’s impact on creative labor, skills, and identities • New frameworks of authorship and attribution • Human–AI collaboration and innovation ecosystems • Copyright, ownership, and ethical dilemmas in AI-generated works • Inclusion, diversity, and bias in AI-mediated creativity more info here: https://lnkd.in/eFichfQz 📅 Key Dates: Submissions open: 15 September 2025 Deadline: 31 January 2026 First-round reviews: Feb–Apr 2026 Workshop: 30 September 2026 👩💻 Guest Editors: Marta Massi (Athabasca University, Canada) Marek Prokupek (KEDGE Business School, France) Marilena Vecco (Burgundy School of Business, France) ➡️ Submit via Technovation’s Editorial Manager, selecting “VSI: AI in the Cultural and Creative Industries.” 📨 Questions? #TechLeadership #AI #ArtificialIntelligence #Humanities #Ethics #Innovation #FutureofWork #CriticalThinking #Leadership #Technology Read Full Article Here: https://lnkd.in/gQSpjEMc. results.title: Artificial Intelligence and Culture
results.content: The Report is structured into seven thematic sections, offering a global, multidisciplinary perspective: • Ethical landscape of AI in culture • Cultural rights in the digital age • AI and cultural value chains in the creative economy • AI and cultural education • Culture, climate and environmental sustainability • Heritage at risk and AI • AI, freedom and sovereignty This Report reflects both academic research and practical experience and is grounded in UNESCO’s evolving normative ecosystem. She is a member of the UNESCO Global Expert Panel on the 2005 Convention on Cultural Expressions and as part of this role, she has delivered global research and advisory support to state parties on emerging technologies (including AI) in the global creative industries. She is a member of UNESCO’s Global Reference Group on Diversity of Cultural Expressions in the Digital Environment - supporting the development of frameworks for supporting the sector in the age of technologies like AI.

results.title: How do cultural and creative industries shape wellbeing? A ...
results.content: While acknowledging that the value of culture and creativity, hence of CCI, goes far beyond their instrumental value in achieving other ends, this paper will focus on the latter, but considering a broad sphere of effects, i.e., multidimensional wellbeing, which to some extent indirectly captures the intrinsic value of culture through subjective wellbeing and life satisfaction. The European Union, in the framework of the previous European agenda for culture, categorised six spillover effects of CCI on the rest of society and the economy, including innovation and productivity, education and lifelong learning, social innovation and wellbeing, tourism and branding, environmental sustainability and regional development (European Union, 2012). It has been found that, although studies on cultural relations are abundant–albeit usually from partial and localised perspectives– (especially in areas such as health, subjective wellbeing and community building), research on the effects of CCI in particular, and from a more macro perspective, has mainly focused on their economic impact, with significant gaps remaining in other areas (refer back to Table 1).
